author: John Chrysostom
addressee: The congregation in Antioch celebrating the feast of Christ's Nativity
occasion: Preached on the feast of the Nativity, recently introduced at Antioch, to a large crowd; Chrysostom defends the date of the feast and prepares the people for worthy reception of Communion.
argument: Chrysostom celebrates the newly established feast of Christ's Nativity and defends its December date. He argues from the rapid spread of the feast, from the Gospel census under Augustus, and from the timing of Zechariah's service in the Holy of Holies that Christ was conceived after Elizabeth's sixth month and born nine months later in the present month. He then answers pagan and Manichaean mockery of the Incarnation by showing that God is not defiled by dwelling in pure flesh, any more than the sun is defiled by its rays touching filth. Finally, he exhorts the congregation to approach the Eucharist with fear, purity, and orderly reverence.

outline.move: Chrysostom rejoices that the long-awaited Nativity feast has now arrived and praises the congregation's zeal in filling the church.
He offers the first proof of the feast's date: its rapid spread and growth show it is from God, like the Gospel preaching.
He presents the second proof from the census of Augustus, which brought Joseph and Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem, fulfilling prophecy.
He explains how God used the census to move Mary to Bethlehem and begins a longer proof from the Jewish temple and its liturgy.
He describes the tabernacle as a type of the cosmos, with the veil separating the outer sanctuary from the Holy of Holies.
He shows from Scripture that the high priest entered the Holy of Holies alone and only once a year, on the tenth of the seventh month.
He identifies that occasion as the Feast of Tabernacles, when Zechariah received the angel's announcement about John.
He calculates from Elizabeth's conception after the month of Gorpiaios that Mary conceived in the sixth month, Dystros, and that Christ was born nine months later in the present month.
He refutes pagan and Manichaean mockery of the Incarnation, arguing that God is not defiled by taking pure flesh.
He urges the congregation to approach the Eucharist with fear, purity, and orderly reverence, not with pushing and shouting.
He concludes with a final exhortation to reverence in all sacred actions and a doxology.

cast.name: John Chrysostom
cast.who: The preacher and bishop delivering the homily.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: The incarnate Son of God, whose birth is being celebrated.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: The Virgin Mother of Jesus, of Davidic descent.

cast.name: Joseph
cast.who: Mary's betrothed, of the house and lineage of David.

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.who: Wife of Zechariah and mother of John the Baptist.

cast.name: Zechariah
cast.who: Priest and father of John the Baptist, who received the angel's announcement in the temple.

cast.name: John the Baptist
cast.who: Son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Christ.

cast.name: Gabriel
cast.who: The angel who announced John's birth to Zechariah and Jesus' conception to Mary.

cast.name: Augustus
cast.who: Roman emperor whose census decree brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.

cast.name: Quirinius
cast.who: Governor of Syria at the time of the first census.

cast.name: Herod
cast.who: King of Judea in the days of Zechariah.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: Apostle whose writings Chrysostom cites on the tabernacle and the temple of God.

cast.name: Moses
cast.who: Lawgiver through whom God gave the regulations for the tabernacle and the Day of Atonement.

cast.name: Aaron
cast.who: First high priest, whose rod budded in the ark.

cast.name: Gamaliel
cast.who: Jewish teacher whose counsel about the Gospel Chrysostom applies to the feast.

cast.name: Nathanael
cast.who: Israelite who expressed doubt that anything good could come from Nazareth, knowing from prophecy that the Messiah was to come from Bethlehem, not Nazareth.

cast.name: Philip
cast.who: Disciple who told Nathanael he had found Jesus of Nazareth.

cast.name: Nicodemus
cast.who: Jewish leader to whom some said no prophet arises from Galilee.

key_terms.sense: God's saving plan and arrangement, especially the Incarnation
The feast of Christ's birth, the Nativity
The Roman census or registration under Augustus
The innermost sanctuary of the tabernacle or temple, entered only by the high priest once a year
The veil separating the Holy of Holies from the outer sanctuary, also a type of heaven
The Jewish Feast of Tabernacles, when the high priest entered the Holy of Holies
A title for Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, whose rays purify rather than defile
The believer or the body as God's dwelling place, applied to Christ's flesh and to Christians
The sacred mystery of the Eucharist
The offering, especially the Eucharistic sacrifice
The priestly division or order of service to which Zechariah belonged

scripture: Chrysostom cites the Septuagint (LXX) and the Gospels. Psalm numbering follows the LXX. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and LXX Psalm numbering where applicable; for example, LXX Psalm references should be noted as LXX if they differ from the Hebrew numbering.
uncertain: The exact year of the homily is uncertain; it is placed in the late 380s based on Chrysostom's Antiochene ministry.
The precise identity of the 'some from the West' who brought knowledge of the feast to Antioch is not stated.
The exact calendar equivalences between the Macedonian months and modern dates are approximate.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Nathanael: 'Israelite who expressed doubt that anything good could come from Nazareth, knowing from prophecy that the Messiah was to come from Bethlehem, not Nazareth.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐκ Ναζαρὲθ δύναταί τι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι; ὁ Χριστὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ φησιν· Ἴδε ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος οὐκ ἔστι... Ἐπειδὴ οὐ συνηρπάγη τῇ ἀπαγγελίᾳ τοῦ Φιλίππου, ἀλλ' ᾔδει σαφῶς καὶ ἀκριβῶς, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν Ναζαρὲθ, οὔτε ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἔδει τὸν Χριστὸν τεχθῆναι, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ ἐν τῇ Βηθλεέμ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Nathanael expressed doubt that anything good could come from Nazareth; Chrysostom interprets this as showing his knowledge of prophecy that Christ must come from Bethlehem/Judaea, not Nazareth/Galilee. The doubt was his initial response, not a confident assertion of knowledge.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Pagan and Manichaean opponents (paraphrased): 'Introduced by 'φασὶν' ('they say'); sections: ["8", "9"]'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: πολλοὶ τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἀκούοντες, ὅτι Θεὸς ἐτέχθη ἐν σαρκὶ, καταγελῶσι διασύροντες... καὶ πολλοὺς τῶν αἱρετικῶν... Αὐτοὶ γὰρ καὶ εἰς αἰλούρους καὶ κύνας, πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν αἱρετικῶν καὶ εἰς ἔτι τούτων ἀτιμότερα τοῦ Θεοῦ κατάγειν τολμῶσι τὴν οὐσίαν... κἀκεῖνοι μὲν, καὶ οἱ τὰ αὐτὰ ἀσεβοῦντες αὐτοῖς Μανιχαῖοι
_unresolved_facts.fix: The opponents are explicitly identified as 'Greeks' (pagans) in section 8 and 'Manichaeans' in section 9, not introduced merely by 'φασὶν'. The brief should note: 'Greek mockers (section 8) and Manichaean heretics (section 9), introduced by explicit identification.'

_unresolved_facts.claim: An interlocutor (objection): 'Introduced by 'φησὶ' or 'φησίν'; distinct objections occur at different points; sections: ["2", "3", "5"]'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The brief should include section 8 for interlocutor objections: 'Καὶ τί τοῦτο συντελεῖ πρὸς τὴν οἰκονομίαν ταύτην, φησίν;' (section 3) and the extended 'Τί οὖν ταῦτα, φησὶ, πρὸς τὴν προκειμένην ἡμέραν;' (section 5). However, section 2 does not contain a clear interlocutor objection with φησίν; the brief should verify this claim or remove section 2.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Section 4 move: 'He explains how God used the census to move Mary to Bethlehem and begins a longer proof from the Jewish temple and its liturgy.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐντεῦθεν ἡμῖν δῆλόν ἐστιν, ὅτι καὶ ἡ Παρθένος ἐκ γένους ἐστὶ Δαυϊδικοῦ... Ἵνα δὲ σαφεστέραν καὶ γνωριμωτέραν ὑμῖν ἀπόδειξιν παράσχωμαι... Νόμος ἦν παλαιὸς τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις... Ὅτε τῶν Αἰγυπτιακῶν θορύβων...
_unresolved_facts.fix: Section 4 primarily establishes Mary's Davidic descent and then begins the temple/tablernacle typology. The census explanation is largely completed in section 3; section 4's main new contribution is proving Mary's Davidic lineage and transitioning to the temple proof.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Section 8 move: 'He calculates from Elizabeth's conception after the month of Gorpiaios that Mary conceived in the sixth month, Dystros, and that Christ was born nine months later in the present month.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μετὰ δὲ τὸν Γορπιαῖον, ἕκτον μῆνα ἐχούσης τῆς Ἐλισάβετ, ὅσπερ ἐστὶν ὁ Δύστρος, ἤρξατο συλλαμβάνειν λοιπὸν ἡ Μαρία
_unresolved_facts.fix: Mary conceived in Dystros, which was Elizabeth's sixth month, not Mary's sixth month. The brief should clarify: 'Elizabeth's sixth month of pregnancy (Dystros) is when Mary conceived.'
